rfm_tuples.R: 'Currently, healthcare centers and physicians should bill the most recent healthcare policies... we believe the code will transition to CPT code 64582 for the Inspire V procedure, including the use of a -52 modifier. INSP frames the Inspire V coding situation as a manageable transition from 64568 toward 64582 + 52-modifier, with top commercial payers aligned.
rfm_tuples.f: If the coding pathway were stable / clarifying as described, subsequent INSP filings (10-Q, 8-K) would reaffirm 64568/64582 as the operative codes and not introduce more dilutive billing pathways. Adverse guidance from a major coding stakeholder (AHA, AMA, MAC) routing Inspire V to an UNLISTED procedure code (64999) would be a sharply worse outcome than the 10-K describes.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-05-04) discloses: 'in April 2026 the American Hospital Association (AHA) recommended use of CPT code 64999 for Inspire V commercial cases. CPT code 64999 is an unlisted procedure code for the nervous system and is to be used when no specific CPT code exists...' Unlisted-code billing is the worst-case reimbursement scenario — case-by-case pricing, manual review, payer denials.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K's coding narrative was already strained (the -52 modifier admits 10-50% professional-fee reduction), but the company framed 64568→64582 as the path. This is the precise risk the 10-K's risk factor warned about but did not quantify. Reimbursement disintermediation of this magnitude on the company's flagship next-gen product directly explains the ~70% drawdown.

summary: INSP is a profitable, well-capitalized ($404M cash, no debt, clean auditor) commercial-stage medical-device franchise with a real IP estate (115 granted USPTO patents) and clinical-trial spine (STAR PHASE3 + active post-approval studies) — NOT a fraud or distress story. The -70% drawdown is explained by a multi-front commercial-stage reimbursement crisis on the next-gen Inspire V launch: (1) RED FLAG — AHA recommended unlisted CPT 64999 (worst-case billing pathway) in April 2026, far worse than 10-K narrative; (2) SEVERE — new CMS WISeR prior-authorization program adversely impacted Q1 2026 revenue and was not specifically flagged in the 10-K despite starting before its Feb 13 filing; (3) MODERATE — three IPRs filed against asserted patents in Nyxoah dispute plus DOJ AKS CID plus active securities class action. Composite 0.875 weighted across 8 verifiable claims (4 PASS / 2 MOD / 1 SEV / 1 RED).
